title: Macroeconomic analysis: GDP, inflation and rates
objectives: Read GDP, CPI inflation, repo rate and fiscal data.
Link macro variables to sector and stock views.
body_md:
Top-down research starts with the economy.

## What to watch

| Indicator | What it tells you |
|---|---|
| **GDP growth** | Size and speed of the economy; demand for goods and credit |
| **CPI inflation** | Price rise for consumers; RBI targets 4% with a ±2% band |
| **Repo rate** | RBI's policy rate; higher rates raise borrowing costs and bond yields |
| **CRR / SLR** | Reserves banks must hold; they affect liquidity |
| **Fiscal deficit** | Government borrowing; high deficits can crowd out private credit |
| **Current account** | Trade and capital flows; affects the rupee |
| **IIP, PMI** | Industrial and business activity, early signals |

## Cause and effect

- Higher inflation leads the **MPC** to raise rates, which hurts rate-sensitive sectors (real estate, autos, NBFCs) and long bonds.
- A weaker rupee helps exporters (IT, pharma) and hurts importers (oil marketing companies).
- Rising commodity prices squeeze margins of buyers, such as FMCG and paints.

> **Exam tip:** Be ready to say which sector gains or loses from a given macro move.
example: CPI inflation rises above 6% for two quarters. The MPC raises the repo rate. A bank's cost of funds rises, home loans become costlier and demand for housing may soften.
say: Our view assumes a stable repo rate and 6.5% GDP growth; here are the risks.
Macro is context for the stock, not a trading signal alone.
never: GDP is up, so every stock will rise.
Ignore the inflation print, it never matters.

check.why: Repo is the key short-term lending rate.
Exporters earn in foreign currency, so a weaker rupee lifts rupee revenue.

check.q: The CPI inflation target band set for RBI is:
check.why: RBI targets 4% with a tolerance band of ±2%.
